transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My doctor told me I should come in because my weight’s gotten… low. People are making a bigger deal of it than I think they need to. I feel like being lighter helps me keep moving at the shop, honestly. Keeps me from getting slowed down.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
I… yeah, I suppose I am. If I eat something heavy, or those holiday foods we used to make, I start thinking right away that I’ll gain weight. Like I’ll lose the grip I’ve worked hard to keep.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I eat what I plan to eat. I wouldn’t call it a large amount.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No… I don’t make myself throw up.
Do you limit the types or amounts of food you eat to avoid gaining weight?

Yes… I do. On days I’m in the workshop, I mostly just have tea, maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for a real meal feels… unnecessary, and like it would throw off the control I have over the day.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t call it excessive. I’m on my feet a lot for work, but I’m not, um, going out of my way to exercise.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you thought was excessive in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. Not… not in the way you mean, I guess.
Do you think your weight is currently low, or is that just what other people are telling you?

I think other people are making more of it than it is. My husband says I look too thin, and the apprentices have said things too, but… I feel fine. I think they’re mistaking discipline for being sick.
Do you think your weight is normal for your height?

I think it’s normal enough. Other people—my husband, some of the apprentices—they keep saying I look too thin, but I don’t really see it that way. I feel fine. I think they’re mixing up being disciplined with being sick.
Do you think your appearance is normal when you look in the mirror?
I think I look… normal enough. My husband and the apprentices keep saying I’m too thin, but I don’t really see it. I tell them I’m fine—that they’re mixing up discipline with being sick.
Have you had your menstrual period in the past few months?
I’m not really sure that applies to me anymore… I haven’t kept track of that kind of thing.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?
I don’t know. I mean… I try not to let meals get that way. I wouldn’t really call it losing control.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as being underweight?
Not really. I know they keep saying I look too thin—my husband, the apprentices—but I don’t see it that way. I feel like I’m fine… people just mistake discipline for being sick.
Do you think your weight is lower than what most people would consider normal for someone of your height and build?

I guess… technically, yes. My doctor sent me here because it’s gotten low enough that everyone’s making a fuss. But I don’t really see it as a problem. Being lighter helps me keep moving in the shop, not get slowed down.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that was much larger than most people would eat in a short period of time?
No… I don’t think so. I’m not sitting down and eating some huge amount all at once, if that’s what you mean.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as fat?
No… not exactly fat. I just don’t see what they see. My husband and the apprentices say I’m too thin, but I tell them I’m fine. People confuse being disciplined with being sick.
Do you think your weight is the main thing that determines your self-worth?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t put it that way. I just feel better when I know I’ve kept myself in check. That’s all.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the main thing that determines how you feel about yourself?
I’m not sure. I mean… I notice it, of course. But “main thing” sounds a bit strong. I just feel better when I’m… in control of myself.
Does your fear of gaining weight interfere with your daily life or relationships?

A little, I suppose. If I eat something heavy, or the holiday foods we used to make, I start worrying right away… like I’ll gain weight and lose the grip I’ve worked hard to keep. So I tend to avoid it.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive, even if it was not in a short period of time?
I don’t really know. I mean… “excessive” is hard to say. Sometimes it feels like too much to me, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
